verifications.claim: Millennials are also known as Generation Y.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Millennials, also known as Generation Y or Gen Y" (R1); "Generation Y, also known as Millennials" (R3); "Millennials (also known as Generation Y)" (R7)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly state Millennials are also known as Generation Y.

verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "typically being defined as people born from 1981 to 1996" (R1); "born between 1981 and 1996" (R2); "born between the years 1981 and 1996" (R3); "born between 1981 and 1996" (R4)
verifications.reasoning: Standard definition directly supported by multiple sources.

verifications.claim: Millennials fall between Generation X and Generation Z.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "the demographic cohort following Generation X and preceding Generation Z" (R1); "falls between Generation X and Generation Z" (R3)

verifications.claim: As of 2026, Millennials are roughly 30 to 45 years old.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Born 1981-1996 (multiple); in 2026: 1981 birth year = 45 years old, 1996 = 30 years old
verifications.reasoning: Age range precisely matches standard 1981-1996 birth years for 2026.

verifications.claim: Millennials represent approximately 36% of the U.S. labor force.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "largest labor force share (36%) in the US" (R3); "make up 36% of the workforce in the US" (R8)
verifications.reasoning: Exact figure directly attributed to U.S. labor force/workforce.

verifications.claim: Millennials make up the largest share of the U.S. workforce.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "largest labor force share (36%)" (R3); "36% ... closely followed by Gen X (31%)" (R8)
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm they hold the largest share.

verifications.claim: Millennials are the first generation to come of age in the internet explosion.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Millennials came of age during the internet explosion" (R4); "As adolescents and young adults ... elevated familiarity with the Internet" (R1)
verifications.reasoning: Direct phrasing in R4; supported by R1 description.

verifications.claim: Millennials are often children of Baby Boomers.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Most millennials are the children of baby boomers and older members of Generation X"

verifications.claim: Millennials are now raising Generation Alpha.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "and are often the parents of members of Generation Alpha"

verifications.claim: Millennials are often termed Echo Boomers.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Millennials are sometimes called Echo Boomers" (R1); "also known as ... Echo boomers" (R5, R7)
verifications.reasoning: Directly termed as such in sources.

verifications.claim: Many Millennials faced the Great Recession early in their careers.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "in the wake of the Great Recession"; "suffered significant economic disruption since starting their working lives"
verifications.reasoning: Directly links Great Recession to early working lives.
